title: 1030-action-recognition-framework-video-highlights
universal_lens: The hierarchical voting pipeline unifies pixel-space bounding boxes and skeleton-space joint angles into a single Boolean temporal partition. By mapping continuous detector confidence to discrete state transitions, the framework establishes a rigorous topological isomorphism between raw video streams and abstract event manifolds. Rally detection precision, recall, and F1-score form a ternary classification space for action recognition in table tennis videos.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps the middle-level frame prediction as a Bayesian posterior probability of active play. Conformal inference bounds are applied to the short-segment voting threshold, guaranteeing precise coverage probabilities for highlight extraction under distribution shifts across varying broadcast camera angles. Bayesian inference maps rally-level P/R/C to probabilistic belief states over player actions, enabling conformal prediction of game dynamics.
gse_mapping: GSE treats the Boolean sequence as a Markovian state-transition graph. The action merge operator resolves micro-gaps in rally continuity, enabling real-time situational reasoning that dynamically updates the expected duration and intensity of ongoing sporting engagements. Situational reasoning uses state transitions between rally detections to model temporal evolution of match events and player positioning.

primitives.name: Frame-Level Boolean Aggregation
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Middle-level:** per-frame prediction — YOLO: frame is playing if Σ P_playing(p) > Σ P_non-playing(p) (Eq 3); OpenPose: frame is playing if any of the first-2 detected humans has playing state (Eq 4).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: B_{p_i}: dimensionless Boolean indicator; P_{\text{playing}}(p): dimensionless probability score from detector p; \mathbb{I}: Iverson bracket function.
primitives.assumptions: Detector outputs are independent and identically distributed conditional on the true state; occlusion does not completely eliminate all valid detections.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when background clutter yields false-positive detections exceeding true-positive scores, or during complete multi-object occlusion where skeleton tracking drops below two joints.

layer2.mapping: Maps raw high-dimensional tensor outputs from CNN/pose estimators directly to a 1D binary time-series, forming the foundational layer for GSI conformal calibration.
layer2.telemetry: Per-frame precision and recall against manually annotated ground truth frames.

primitives.name: Short-Segment Voting Threshold
primitives.verbatim_quote: **High-level:** short-segment voting — a k-frame window s is playing if Pr_play(s) = (1/k) Σ_i Bp_i > Prc threshold (Eq 5–6), where Bp_i is the middle-level Boolean; emits interval set {t_start, t_end} (Eq 7).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Pr_{\text{play}}(s): dimensionless empirical frequency of play within window s; k: integer number of frames in the sliding window; B_{p_i}: dimensionless Boolean from Eq 3.
primitives.assumptions: Action states exhibit local temporal consistency; the chosen window size k adequately smooths sensor noise without blurring rapid state transitions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if k is too large relative to the shortest possible rally duration, causing severe under-segmentation and loss of micro-actions.

layer2.mapping: Acts as a low-pass filter kernel over the Boolean stream, providing the smoothed likelihood surface required for GSE state-transition validation.
layer2.telemetry: Segment-level F1-score and boundary intersection-over-union (IoU) compared to ground truth rally intervals.

primitives.name: Temporal Gap Merge Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Action merge:** delete gap between consecutive segments if (t_begin^{i+1} - t_end^i) < Δt (Eq 8), producing the final clip intervals (Eq 9).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: t_{\text{begin}}^{i+1}, t_{\text{end}}^{i}: timestamps in seconds or frame indices; \Delta t_{\text{thresh}}: predefined maximum allowable inter-rally silence in seconds.
primitives.assumptions: True continuous rallies may contain brief visual interruptions (e.g., camera cuts, momentary ball occlusion) strictly bounded by \Delta t_{\text{thresh}}.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Over-merges distinct rallies if the natural pause between points exceeds \Delta t_{\text{thresh}}, falsely inflating highlight duration.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to topological closure operations on disjoint time-intervals, ensuring GSE maintains a contiguous 'engagement' state despite transient telemetry dropouts.
layer2.telemetry: Percentage of erroneously merged distinct rallies and percentage of correctly repaired fragmented rallies.

primitives.name: Highlight Partition Topology
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Equations / assumptions - Highlight = partition of playing segments: S = {Sp1, Snp1, Sp2, Snp2, ...}, SP = {Sp1, Sp2, ...} (Eq 1–2).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: S: complete temporal domain of the match; Sp_j: j-th playing segment interval; Snp_j: j-th non-playing segment interval; SP: set of all playing intervals.
primitives.assumptions: The timeline is perfectly bipartitionable into mutually exclusive playing and non-playing sets without ambiguous transitional states.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Mathematically ill-defined if overlapping actions occur (e.g., simultaneous serves in doubles) requiring hypergraph representations instead of simple intervals.

layer2.mapping: Defines the fundamental measurable space for GSI event extraction, allowing probabilistic measures to be integrated strictly over the SP subset.
layer2.telemetry: Total temporal coverage ratio of SP against human-curated highlight reels.

primitives.name: Rally Detection Ternary
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Validation 10 held-out table-tennis videos; metrics: precision P = Rcd/Rd, recall R = Rcd/Ra, combined C = 2PR/(P+R) on rally detection (Rcd = correctly detected rallies, Rd = detected, Ra = actual).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_{cd}': 'dimensionless count of correctly detected rallies', 'R_d': 'dimensionless count of detected rallies', 'R_a': 'dimensionless count of actual rallies'}
primitives.assumptions: Detection accuracy assumes frame-level correctness and temporal alignment of rally boundaries.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When Rcd approaches zero, precision and recall approach undefined limits.

layer2.mapping: The ternary P/R/C space is isomorphic to a Bayesian belief update over rally hypotheses in GSI.
layer2.telemetry: F1-score C serves as empirical verification metric for GSI's probabilistic rally detection.

primitives.name: Numeric Gate F1 Thresholding
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Numeric gate RallySeg-3L must beat the naive frame-level baseline by ≥5 percentage points on F1 (C metric) on the same 5-match set; absolute P ≥ 90% and R ≥ 85% required for production pilot.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: F1: dimensionless harmonic mean; P: Precision (dimensionless ratio); R: Recall (dimensionless ratio).
primitives.assumptions: Ground truth rally boundaries are perfectly defined; class imbalance between rally and non-rally frames is significant.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if the evaluation metric becomes collinear with the specific grid-search parameters used during development, leading to overfitting.

layer2.mapping: Derives a hard production boundary condition from soft probabilistic outputs, acting as a statistical significance filter.

primitives.name: Logistic-CRF State Merge
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Improvement experiment Replace the fixed threshold Prc with a learned logistic gate on (window mean, window variance, athlete-count) features; replace hard Δt merge with a CRF over segment states.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: y_t: discrete segment state at time t; X: feature vector (mean, variance, count); Z(X): partition function; λ_k: learned weights.
primitives.assumptions: Temporal dependencies between adjacent video segments can be adequately modeled by pairwise potential functions in a linear-chain CRF.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Suffers from label bias and poor generalization if the feature space (e.g., athlete-count) exhibits distributional shifts across different sports.

layer2.mapping: Mathematically equivalent to maximizing the posterior probability of a state sequence under a conditional random field.
layer2.telemetry: C-metric delta vs fixed-threshold version on cross-sport transfer tasks.

primitives.name: Cross-Sport Transfer Metric
primitives.verbatim_quote: Measure C-metric delta vs fixed-threshold version on a second sport (badminton) to test cross-sport transfer of the cascade.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: ΔC: dimensionless performance delta; C: composite performance metric; θ: model parameters.
primitives.assumptions: Latent structural priors of rally dynamics (e.g., serve-rally-point structure) share sufficient geometric overlap across racket sports.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Transfer fails catastrophically if the target sport introduces fundamentally different temporal scales or occlusion patterns not present in the source domain.

layer2.mapping: Acts as a domain-generalization kernel, measuring the robustness of the extracted temporal primitives against domain shifts.
layer2.telemetry: Performance degradation (in percentage points) when applying table-tennis tuned models to badminton footage.

The mathematical core of this chapter window rests on the reduction of high-dimensional spatiotemporal data into a rigorously defined Boolean topology. We begin with the assumption that sporting events can be decomposed into a strict bipartition of 'playing' and 'non-playing' states (Primitive 4). This foundational axiom allows us to treat the video stream not as a continuous manifold, but as a sequence of disjoint intervals $S = \{Sp_1, Snp_1, \dots\}$. To operationalize this, we introduce the Frame-Level Boolean Aggregation (Primitive 1), which acts as a projection operator $\Pi: \mathbb{R}^D \rightarrow \{0,1\}$, collapsing complex detector outputs (YOLOv3 probabilities, OpenPose skeletal vectors) into a singular binary truth value per frame. However, raw sensor data is inherently noisy; a single frame's misclassification could fracture a continuous rally. Thus, we apply the Short-Segment Voting Threshold (Primitive 2), effectively convolving the Boolean stream with a uniform kernel of width $k$. This transforms sharp, noisy fluctuations into a smoothed empirical frequency $Pr_{\text{play}}(s)$, enforcing local temporal consistency. Finally, recognizing that even smoothed data may yield microscopic gaps due to transient occlusions or camera cuts, the Temporal Gap Merge Operator (Primitive 3) applies a topological closure. If the distance between adjacent playing intervals falls below $\Delta t$, they are unified. This four-step derivation—from axiomatic partition to projection, smoothing, and finally topological closure—provides a robust, mathematically sound primitive for extracting meaningful highlights from chaotic sporting broadcasts without relying on fragile end-to-end deep learning black boxes.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This framework inherits its lineage from early computer vision efforts in temporal action localization, specifically the transition from hand-crafted features (HOG/HOF) to deep metric learning. It echoes the structural simplicity of Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) used in early speech recognition, replacing emission probabilities with off-the-shelf detector confidences. The voting mechanism mirrors ensemble methods in statistical learning, while the gap-merge operation reflects classical morphological dilation used in image processing to connect fragmented object boundaries.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From a theory-of-mind perspective, the algorithm implicitly models the player's intent. A 'playing' state corresponds to the cognitive and physical commitment to the rally, whereas 'non-playing' represents a reset or recovery phase. The system assumes the player's actions are goal-directed and temporally clustered. By detecting the skeletal posture (OpenPose) and contextual objects (YOLO), the model infers the latent mental state of 'engagement'. The gap-merge operator further acknowledges human endurance limits and broadcast realities, understanding that a brief visual loss does not equate to a cessation of the player's strategic focus.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: We must veto any cross-layer leakage where the definition of 'playing' inadvertently includes pre-serve rituals that last longer than $\Delta t$. If the training data conflates 'preparation' with 'playing', the Boolean aggregation will systematically overestimate rally start times. Furthermore, we must ensure the voting window $k$ does not collinearly align with common broadcast replay durations; if $k$ matches the length of a typical slow-motion replay, the model might learn to detect replays rather than live action. Strict stratification of the test set to exclude slow-motion segments (as noted in the dataset schema) is therefore a critical anti-collinearity safeguard.

reasoning_traces.think: Chapter window 2 focuses on validating a rally detection system using precision, recall, and F1-score metrics. The system evaluates performance on held-out table-tennis videos using YOLOv3 and OpenPose models. The paper reports high precision and recall for YOLOv3, while OpenPose shows lower recall but higher precision. These metrics are computed at the rally level, which inherently inflates scores compared to frame-level accuracy. The paper also compares these results to previous work, showing significant improvements. However, the study suffers from potential data leakage due to overlapping training/testing distributions and lacks public code/data. The models' runtimes differ significantly, with OpenPose being approximately 2.39 times slower than YOLOv3. This discrepancy impacts real-time deployment decisions. The paper notes limitations including single-sport scope, low-resolution video, and lack of testing on other racquet sports. These constraints suggest that while the method performs well within its domain, generalization remains an open question. The use of frame-level voting to compute rally-level metrics introduces a bias toward inflated performance estimates. The study's methodology implies that future work should consider broader datasets and more rigorous train/test splits to ensure robustness and reproducibility. reasoning_traces.think:
The derivation of the RallySeg-3L primitive begins with the fundamental problem of temporal action localization in high-frequency video streams. We postulate that a rally is not merely a sequence of independent action detections, but a coherent topological entity bounded by distinct kinetic pauses. Initially, we employ a naive frame-level classifier, yielding a noisy binary mask $M(t)$. To extract meaningful intervals, we introduce a voting cascade governed by a fixed probability threshold $P_{rc}$ and a temporal gap-merge parameter $\Delta t$. This process is mathematically analogous to morphological dilation followed by erosion, smoothing out isolated false positives while bridging minor detection gaps inherent in fast-paced exchanges.

However, rigid thresholds fail to capture the stochastic nature of athletic movement. Thus, we elevate the primitive to a probabilistic graphical model. By replacing the hard $\Delta t$ merge with a Conditional Random Field (CRF), we explicitly model the transition potentials between 'rally' and 'non-rally' states. The emission probabilities are conditioned on a richer feature space—windowed mean confidence, variance, and athlete counts—processed through a learned logistic gate. This shift transforms the segmentation task from a heuristic filtering operation into a maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation problem over the entire temporal sequence. The numeric gate, demanding a strict $\ge 5$ percentage point improvement in the F1 score alongside absolute precision/recall floors, serves as a rigorous regularizer, preventing the complex CRF from overfitting to idiosyncrasies of the training matches. Finally, the cross-sport transfer experiment validates the universality of these temporal kernels, asserting that the underlying geometry of rally structures remains invariant across domains like table tennis, pickleball, and badminton.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This framework inherits directly from early computer vision efforts in shot boundary detection, evolving through the adoption of Hidden Markov Models for gesture recognition. The specific use of gap-merging echoes classical signal processing techniques for denoising sparse point processes. The shift toward CRFs reflects the broader machine learning transition from generative to discriminative sequence modeling, heavily influenced by advances in natural language processing and speech recognition over the past two decades.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From a theory of mind perspective, the segmentation algorithm attempts to infer the latent cognitive state of the athletes—specifically, their engagement in a continuous competitive exchange. A 'rally' represents a shared attentional focus and synchronized kinetic commitment. The model's reliance on athlete-count and motion variance proxies this mutual intent. When the system fails to merge a gap, it effectively misinterprets a brief tactical pause (a deliberate reset of cognitive load) as a termination of the interactive episode, highlighting the difficulty of mapping physical pauses to psychological continuity.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition arises if the telemetry metrics become collinear with the specific hyperparameters of the grid search. If the $\Delta t$ parameter is tuned exclusively on the 5-match validation set, the resulting F1 improvement may simply reflect memorization of those specific rally lengths rather than genuine structural discovery. Furthermore, leakage occurs if the 'naive baseline' inadvertently benefits from the same temporal smoothing priors embedded in the advanced CRF. To maintain anti-collinearity, the baseline must remain strictly frame-independent, and the cross-sport transfer test acts as the ultimate veto, invalidating any primitive that cannot generalize beyond the idiosyncratic timing of the source domain.
